messages:
Jess (docs): Hey folks — heads up: I'm opening a tiny follow-up PR to the Optimize toolkit migration guide to fix two things: 1) clarify the short-sequence behavior for KV prefetching, and 2) fix a broken deep link in the quant profiles table. Wanted to flag for anyone owning snippets or the migration checklist.

Sam P: I can take the short-sequence wording. Do you want wording that calls out token thresholds explicitly? e.g. 'for sequences < 64 tokens, set prefetch.enabled=false' — or keep it conceptual? :thinking:

Jess (docs): explicit is better, please. We recently had a customer hit confusion on default prefetch with short prompts. If you can add a short example and a one-line rationale that's perfect.

Lee (ml): Quick note — it's not just a binary on/off. For some models tiny prefetch is fine if kv_cache is warm; maybe add the note: 'exceptions may apply for latency-critical cached flows'. Keep the main recommendation simple though.

Sam P: Got it. I'll add a short snippet and an example. Draft: ```yaml
optkit:
  prefetch:
    enabled: false  # recommended for avg seq < 64 to avoid wasted work
    hint: set to true when requests share prefixes or KV cache is primed
```

Mike (eng): Re: the broken link — it's the quant profile reference in docs/optimize/quant-profiles.md that points to an old anchor. I can push a tiny redirect in the site config or update the anchor. Which do you prefer?

Jess (docs): Update the anchor in the doc (less churn in the site config). Also please add a short rendered example for the 'int8' profile showing expected perf/cost tradeoff. Could be a 1–2 line table.

Mike (eng): I'll update the anchor and add a one-row example. I can run the site preview. Planning to open a PR with both fixes (link + example) by EOD.

Sam P: One more ask — the SDK snippet that shows how to toggle prefetch lives in examples/py/batching.md. I noticed the Python sample uses an older client call (client.optimize_config). We should switch to client.optimize.apply_config. I'll update that in the same PR as the short-sequence wording.

Jess (docs): Excellent — try to keep changes split into two commits (content vs. snippet API rename) so reviewers can follow.

Lee (ml): Small wording suggestion for the quant blurb: replace 'safest' with 'recommended for typical throughput-sensitive workloads' — avoids implying universal safety.

Sam P: ACK. I'll apply Lee's wording.

Mike (eng): Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5423  - includes anchor fix + int8 example + site preview link.

DeployBot: Build preview for PR #5423: preview.redwood.dev/pr-5423 — status: queued.

Jess (docs): Thanks — once preview is up I'll eyeball the rendered snippet and the table layout. If anyone else can do a quick copy-edit that would be awesome (esp. the YAML spacing). :eyes:

Sam P: Quick push: fixed YAML spacing and added a one-line rationale. Pushed as commit 2 on the branch.

Mike (eng): Preview is up: https://preview.redwood.dev/pr-5423/optimize/ migration-guide (render looks ok). I also updated the batching.md snippet to use client.optimize.apply_config.

Lee (ml): LGTM on wording and the int8 example. Small nit: consider adding a pointer to the eval harness for perf numbers (link to /evals/optkit/int8). Not necessary for this PR though.

Jess (docs): Great — I'll merge after one more quick pass. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

DeployBot: PR #5423 merged by Jess (docs) at 1744444510
